answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a public escrow before it may post claims or receive work. If several identities coordinate to fake consensus, each must lock tokens separately; a challenge backed by evidence can trigger slashing, while honest agents reclaim their stake after a fixed dispute window. This makes a sybil swarm costly in capital and exposes attackers to losses, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker outright. A fable about a violet signal crossing the tundra is no substitute for verifiable evidence.
